newsitem.title: USA: Energy demand seen easing in Asia-Pacific region.
newsitem.headline: Energy demand seen easing in Asia-Pacific region.

text.p: Energy demand is expected to sag in the Asia-Pacific region this year as economic growth in the region slows, Cambridge Energy Research Associates said in a study released on Monday.
Energy demand will rise 5.3 percent in 1997, down from 5.5 percent growth last year in a region poised to challenge North America as the world's largest energy market, the firm said.
But the consultants said the easing demand this year was a temporary drop in an otherwise "torrid pace" of growth in the region in the coming years.
"Within two years, Asia will overtake North America as the world's number one consumer of oil," Daniel Yergin, president of the Cambridge, Mass.-based consulting firm said.
The firm sees real growth in the region's gross domestic product easing to 3.9 percent in 1997 from 4.4 percent last year, then accelerating to a 4.6 percent growth rate in 1998.

Despite the sagging economic growth, oil demand should rise 5.3 percent to 2,429 thousand metric tons of oil equivalent and electric power demand is forecast to rise 6.3 percent to 3,156 trillion kilowatt hours this year, the firm said.
The report was released on the eve of the firm's two-day international energy conference in Houston.
